mainEntity.name: Can you retexture over an existing ceiling texture without scraping it first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Applying new texture directly over existing texture depends on the current material and its condition. You can rarely spray a light texture directly over thick, brittle textures like heavy popcorn because the added moisture and weight can cause the original material to peel, sag, or fail entirely. However, low-profile textures like light orange peel can sometimes be covered if the surface is cleaned, primed, and skim-coated with a thin joint compound first. The practical tradeoff is preparation time: scraping down to the bare drywall requires more labor up front, but it guarantees that the new texture bonds permanently without bubbling or delaminating.
acceptedAnswer.description: Direct retexturing works only over low-profile finishes after skim-coating. Heavy or popcorn textures must be scraped first to prevent moisture and weight from peeling the ceiling.
